title: First visit to an anchor state
statement: Let $M$ and $M_0$ be machines with the same number of work tapes and state set, and let $q_a$ be a state. Suppose their transition rules agree at every state other than $q_a$, and that $M_0$ at $q_a$ makes a stationary, silent transition back to $q_a$. For a configuration $c$ and time $T$, if the run of $M_0$ from $c$ is in state $q_a$ at time $T$, then some $t\le T$ has the property that the run of $M$ is never in state $q_a$ at any earlier time and its configuration at time $t$ equals the configuration of $M_0$ at time $T$.
hypotheses_covered: Machines $M,M_0$ with the same number of work tapes and state set
Transition rules agree at every state other than $q_a$
At $q_a$, $M_0$ makes the specified stationary silent self-loop
The run of $M_0$ from $c$ is in state $q_a$ at time $T$
replaced:
Let two transition tables agree away from an anchor state, which the second
(stopped) table turns into a silent self-loop. If the stopped run from $c$
stands at the anchor at time $T$, then there is a time $t \le T$ such that the
active run never visits the anchor before $t$ and its time-$t$ configuration
equals the stopped run's time-$T$ configuration.
